facts.big: I’ve played tennis since I was ten
facts.label: Since e for
facts.sub: Use since + ponto de partida e for + duração com o present perfect: I’ve played since ten, I’ve worked here for two years. Pergunte com How long have you…?

facts.label: Desde + ponto no tempo
facts.sub: Use since com um ponto de partida: since March, since Monday, since I was ten. O verbo fica no present perfect: I’ve lived here since March. Em português usamos o presente, mas em inglês não.

facts.label: Há + tempo de duração
facts.sub: Use for com uma duração: for two years, for a long time, for ten minutes. Exemplo: I’ve worked here for two years. Não use since com duração, nem for com ponto de partida.

compare.ask: I’ve played tennis since I was ten.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “jogo tênis desde os dez anos”, com o verbo no presente.
compare.tip: Diga: “I’ve played tennis since I was ten.”
compare.us: Em inglês, usamos o present perfect: I’ve played tennis since I was ten. Since marca o começo e for marca a duração.

paragraphs: It is a sunny morning in Boston. Clara has come to a sports park. She has played tennis since she was ten. Dee has worked here for two years. The tennis court is quiet at this hour. Clara has a big question for the coach.

“Welcome to the park, Clara. Have you played tennis for a long time?” says Dee. “Yes, I’ve played tennis since I was ten. My uncle taught me.” says Clara. “Nice! I’ve been here since March, and I haven’t played much yet.” says Dee.
